extraction.name: Natural Questions
extraction.description: A question answering dataset built from real anonymized, aggregated Google search queries, where annotators label long and short answers on associated Wikipedia pages. The public release includes training, development, and test examples with single or multi-way annotations.
extraction.creator: Tom Kwiatkowski, Jennimaria Palomaki, Olivia Redfield, Michael Collins, Ankur Parikh, Chris Alberti, Danielle Epstein, Illia Polosukhin, Jacob Devlin, Kenton Lee, Kristina Toutanova, Llion Jones, Matthew Kelcey, Ming-Wei Chang, Andrew M. Dai, Jakob Uszkoreit, Quoc Le, Slav Petrov
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Questions were collected from Google Search queries that were 8 words or longer and issued by multiple users in a short period of time; the dataset pairs these with Wikipedia pages and annotated long/short answers, with NULL allowed when no answer exists on the page.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Both long and short answers were set to NULL when no viable answer candidates existed on the Wikipedia page.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of question, Wikipedia page, long answer, and short answer quadruples; the questions come from Google search queries and the evidence documents are Wikipedia pages.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotation was performed with a custom annotation interface by a pool of around 50 annotators; quality evaluation used post hoc correctness checks of non-null answers under consensus judgments from four experts and k-way annotations on a subset of the data.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotation quality was evaluated using post hoc correctness of non-null answers with consensus judgments from four experts, yielding a measure of annotation precision, and using 25-way annotations on a subset of the data to provide insights into recall.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 25 annotations per item on a subset of the data
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may be biased by its reliance on Wikipedia as the evidence source, by filtering for longer queries and excluding many shorter or "how to" queries, and by restricting examples to questions with a Wikipedia page in the top 5 Google search results.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to factual, longer natural-language queries matched with Wikipedia pages in the top 5 search results; it excludes many non-factual, ambiguous, opinion-seeking, shorter, and "how to" questions, and some answerable cases are marked no-answer when evidence is spread across multiple paragraphs or not contained in a single allowed HTML element.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper frames the dataset as having practical utility for users and as a benchmark to drive advances in natural language understanding through real information-seeking question answering.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains real user search queries that were anonymized and aggregated.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Intended as a benchmark dataset for question answering research, especially large-scale end-to-end training and evaluation of QA systems on long-answer and short-answer prediction from Wikipedia pages.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions were sampled and filtered using heuristics from Google search queries, and only question-Wikipedia page pairs were kept when a Wikipedia page appeared in the top 5 search results.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Simple heuristics were used to filter natural-language questions from anonymized aggregated search queries; only queries of 8 words or more were considered, and linguistic tools were used to identify part-of-speech tags and entities.

name.evidence: This paper introduces Natural Questions (NQ), a new data set for QA research

description.evidence: We present the Natural Questions corpus, a question answering data set. Questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine. An annotator is presented with a question along with a Wikipedia page from the top 5 search results, and annotates a long answer ... and a short answer ...

inLanguage.evidence: Questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine. An annotator is presented with a question along with a Wikipedia page

isLiveDataset.evidence: The public release consists of 307,373 training examples with single annotations; 7,830 examples with 5-way annotations for development data; and a further 7,842 examples with 5-way annotated sequestered as test data.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: All the questions in NQ are queries of 8 words or more that have been issued to the Google search engine by multiple users in a short period of time.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: All the questions in NQ are queries of 8 words or more that have been issued to the Google search engine by multiple users in a short period of time.

rai:dataCollectionMissingData.evidence: Both the long and short answer can be NULL if no viable candidates exist on the Wikipedia page.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Natural Questions contains (question, wikipedia page, long answer, short answer) quadruples

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Annotation is performed using a custom annota- tion interface, by a pool of around 50 annotators, with an average annotation time of 80 seconds. ... We use a combination of two methods: 1) post hoc evaluation of correctness of non-null answers, under consensus judgments from four ‘experts’; ... 2) k-way annotations (with k = 25) on a subset of the data.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: Annotation is performed using a custom annota- tion interface

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: We use a combination of two methods: 1) post hoc evaluation of correctness of non-null answers, under consensus judgments from four ‘experts’; ... 2) k-way annotations (with k = 25) on a subset of the data. Post hoc evaluation of non-null answers leads directly to a measure of annotation precision. ... 25-way annotated data provide useful insights into recall

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: k-way annotations (with k = 25) on a subset of the data

rai:dataBiases.evidence: “We focus on Wikipedia as it is a very important source of factual information... however, like any data set there may be biases in this choice. Future data collection efforts may introduce shorter queries, ‘how to’ questions, or domains other than Wikipedia.”

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: “All the questions in NQ are queries of 8 words or more...”; “We focus on longer queries as they are more complex”; “Future data collection efforts may introduce shorter queries, ‘how to’ questions, or domains other than Wikipedia.”; “annotators mark ‘no answer’ if the page does not answer the question, or if the information is present but not contained in a single one of the allowed elements.”

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: “Open-domain question answering (QA) is a benchmark task in natural language understanding (NLU), which has significant utility to users”

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: “Questions consist of real anonymized, aggregated queries issued to the Google search engine.”

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: “We propose NQ as a new benchmark for research in QA.”; “Our goals are three-fold: 1) To provide large-scale end-to-end training data for the QA problem.”; “The public release consists of 307,373 training examples... 7,830 examples... for development data; and a further 7,842 examples... as test data.”

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: From these queries, we sample a subset that either: ... We run questions through the Google search engine and keep those where there is a Wikipedia page in the top 5 search results.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Simple heuristics are used to filter questions from the query stream... All the questions in NQ are queries of 8 words or more... Part of speech tags and entities are identified using Google’s Cloud NLP API.
